scope.description: A three-voter in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores, RestoreCommittedLogs, a low snapshot threshold and small trailing-log retention: one node snapshots, a configuration change adds a non-voter, traffic advances the node's staged commit index past that entry, the node is shut down, the cluster commits eighty more entries while that node is gone, and the node is then restarted from its stores. The probe records the recovered configuration, the node's snapshot index and the leader's snapshot index before the wait, then waits for the configuration in force to be restored and records the resulting configuration, snapshot index and last log index.
assumptions: Cluster, transports, log stores and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.
The node's shutdown and restart are the ordinary public operations used elsewhere in this harness; no bytes are removed or altered.
The leader's log is expected to have been compacted past the restarted node's next index, which is what makes an installed snapshot the only way to catch the node up.

basis.prefix: Start a three-peer cluster with commit-tracking stores, RestoreCommittedLogs and snapshot threshold twenty with trailing logs five; apply ten commands; snapshot the node under test; commit AddNonvoter for a late joiner; apply five more commands so the node's staged commit index passes that entry; record its last log index and shut it down; apply eighty more commands on the leader so it snapshots and compacts; restart the node with NewRaft on a fresh transport and rewire; emit the setup event with the configuration in force, whether the late joiner is in it, whether the recovered configuration has it, the recovered length, the recorded last log index, the node's snapshot index after restart and the leader's latest snapshot index; wait, bounded by twenty seconds, for the late joiner to appear in the node's configuration and emit the result event with the repaired flag, the configuration after the wait and the snapshot and last log indexes after the wait.
basis.requirement: A node whose recovered configuration is behind the configuration in force must regain the configuration in force when the leader can only catch it up with an installed snapshot.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the node's configuration is loaded by its own recovery and updated by the snapshots and entries it receives.

comparisons.description: The node regains the configuration in force after the leader catches it up.
The restoration arrives with an installed snapshot, which the node's snapshot index shows.
